Green olives warmed with preserved lemon, cumin and chilli, with smoked almonds roasted in olive oil and salt.

Filo triangles filled with beef mince spiced with cinnamon, cumin and coriander, brushed with butter and baked until crisp.
the days in Paris that Rick and Ilsa will always have

Light choux puffs beaten with gruyère, Dijon and black pepper, baked until hollow, crisp and golden, served warm from the oven. Heat the oven to 200C. Bring 250ml water, 100g butter and half a tsp salt to the boil. Tip in 150g plain flour and beat over the heat until the dough pulls from the sides. Cool 5 minutes. Beat in 4 eggs one at a time, then 120g grated gruyère, 1 tsp Dijon and pepper. Pipe or spoon 24 small mounds onto lined trays, sprinkle with 30g more gruyère and bake 22 to 25 minutes until puffed and golden.
M: a Moroccan supper away from the café
Chicken thighs braised with onion, ginger, saffron, preserved lemon and green olives until tender, couscous on the side.
Lamb and apricot tagine with couscous
the souk outside the doors of Rick's café

Lamb shoulder braised slowly with ras el hanout, cinnamon, dried apricots and honey, scattered with toasted almonds and coriander, over buttered couscous. Brown 1.2kg diced lamb shoulder in oil in batches. Fry 2 sliced onions for 5 minutes, add 3 garlic cloves, 2 tsp grated ginger, 2 tbsp ras el hanout and 1 cinnamon stick. Pour in 400g tinned tomatoes and 500ml stock, return the lamb, cover and simmer 1.5 hours. Add 150g dried apricots and 1 tbsp honey and cook 30 minutes more. Pour 300ml boiling stock over 300g couscous with 30g butter, cover 5 minutes, fluff. Top the tagine with 50g toasted flaked almonds and coriander.
W: a sweet from the Casablanca bakeries
Moist almond meal cake soaked in an orange and orange blossom syrup, served with thick yoghurt.
K: poured from a height at Rick's
Green tea brewed with a big handful of fresh mint and sugar, poured high into small glasses so it froths.

s.note: the bar at Rick's Café Américain
s.how: Warm 300g green olives in 60ml olive oil with the chopped rind of 1 preserved lemon, 1 tsp ground cumin and a pinch of chilli for 5 minutes. Toss 150g almonds with 1 tbsp oil and salt and roast at 180C for 8 minutes. Serve both warm in small bowls.

s.note: Moroccan street pastries from the Casablanca markets
s.how: Fry 400g beef mince with 1 onion, 1 tsp cinnamon, 1 tsp cumin and salt until browned, then stir in chopped coriander. Cut 8 sheets filo into long strips, brush with 80g melted butter, add a spoonful of filling and fold into triangles. Bake at 190C for 15 minutes until crisp.

m.note: a Moroccan supper away from the café
m.how: Brown 1kg chicken thighs, then soften 2 onions with a thumb of grated ginger and a pinch of saffron. Return the chicken with 375ml water, the chopped rind of 1 preserved lemon and 150g green olives and simmer 40 minutes. Pour 300g couscous into 375ml boiling stock, cover 5 minutes and fluff.

w.note: a sweet from the Casablanca bakeries
w.how: Beat 4 eggs with 200g sugar until pale, then fold in 250g almond meal, the zest of 2 oranges and 1 tsp baking powder. Bake in a 20cm tin at 170C for 40 minutes. Simmer the juice of 2 oranges with 80g sugar and 1 tsp orange blossom water, pour over the warm cake and serve with Greek yoghurt.

d.note: poured from a height at Rick's
d.how: Rinse 2 tbsp green tea in a teapot with a splash of boiling water and tip it out. Add a big bunch of mint, 4 tbsp sugar and 1L boiling water, brew 4 minutes, then pour from a height into small glasses so it froths.
